The live catalogue is roughly 1,675 products + ~37 active categories + 15 static URLs ≈ 1,730 `<loc>` entries (derived from the source catalogues under the 65-name allowlist, cross-checked against CLAUDE.md's independently stated 'only 15 of its 150 Oral Care products are visible' — my model reproduces 15 exactly). So ~40% of the storefront could disappear from the sitemap and this stays green. It is also the only sitemap-content check: nothing asserts that a `hidden` or `discontinued` product is ABSENT (line 123 only asserts one known-good product is present), nothing asserts every `active` product is present, and nothing asserts the count agrees with `db.product.count({ where: VISIBLE })`. Replace the constant with the actual count read from the database in the same run, so the two figures have to reconcile.

findings.title: The WhatsApp preview still shows no price for ~98% of products
findings.detail: The module header (lines 8-11) states the defect this file exists to fix: 'produced the generic homepage card with no photo, no name and no price.' Name and photo are fixed. Price is only ever present when the product has NO supplier description at all, because that is the only branch that includes `$${money(price)}` — 34 of 1,560 live Feel22 rows and 2 of 265 Beesline rows. For everything else the preview shows brand marketing copy and no figure. There are also no `product:price:amount` / `product:price:currency` OG tags to carry it, despite `og:type` being set to `product` (line 62). Appending ' — $X' (or a range, per the AggregateOffer finding) to the summarised description, or adding the OG product price tags, closes it.

findings.title: No aggregateRating, though approved reviews and the computed average already exist
findings.detail: The Product JSON-LD carries no `aggregateRating` and no `review`, so no product is eligible for star rich results. The data is already computed and already public: `index.ts:849` returns `ratingAvg` and `reviewCount` from `reviews: { where: { approved: true } }`, and the page renders `<Stars>` from it (`web/src/pages/Product.tsx:135-137`). Adding it is the honest kind of addition — moderated first-party reviews about the product itself — provided it is emitted ONLY when `reviewCount > 0` (Google rejects `aggregateRating` with `ratingCount: 0`, and an empty rating would be the same shape of unverifiable claim as the old 'Best sellers' rail).

findings.title: 26% of product titles exceed 60 characters; the longest is 189
findings.detail: `titled()` drops the site name when `main.length + tail.length > 60` but never truncates `main` itself. Over the 1,560 live Feel22 rows: **760 (49%) lose the ' · TulipGlam' tail**, and **404 (26%) still exceed 60 characters**, 251 exceed 70. Longest is 189 chars ('Mixa Urea Cica Repair Moisturizing Cream Jar - For Keratosis Pilaris, Dry, Flaky, Strawberry, Rough, & Fragile Skin & Tiny Reddish Bumps With 10% Urea and Niacinamide For Face, Hands & Body'). Half the catalogue therefore has no brand signal in the SERP title and a quarter is truncated mid-phrase by Google; the same string is the WhatsApp preview headline. The comment on line 118 states the 60-char intent, so the code does half of what it says. Use `summarise()`-style word-boundary trimming on `main` before appending the tail.

findings.title: Category head computes a visible-product count and discards it
findings.detail: `include: { parent: true, _count: { select: { products: { where: ctx.visible } } } } }` — `c._count` is never read by the returned object (lines 247-256). It costs a subquery on every category head render and asserts nothing. It is also the only use of `ctx.visible` inside `metaForPath`, so the field looks load-bearing when it is not. The obvious intended guard is missing in two places: a category with zero visible products still returns 200 and indexable here, and `sitemapXml` (line 362) lists **every** `active: true` category with no regard to contents. Not currently realised — every leaf category still holds at least one allowlisted product (thinnest: `skincare-tools` 1, `intimate-care` 4, `toners` 5) — but the allowlist is the owner's to edit and one removal creates an indexed empty shelf. Either use the count (404 or noindex at zero, and skip it in the sitemap) or delete it.

findings.title: Homepage declares @type Store — a physical shop — with no address
findings.detail: `"@type": "Store"` is a `LocalBusiness` subtype, which asserts a place customers can visit. This business holds no stock and has no premises (CLAUDE.md 'Business model — no inventory'), and the only address emitted is `{ "@type": "PostalAddress", addressCountry: "LB" }` (line 173) — no street, no locality. schema.org's `OnlineStore` (a subtype of `OnlineBusiness`, added 2022) says exactly what is true. Same class as the promo-band and 'Best sellers' fixes this codebase already made. Related, smaller: line 171 publishes `settings.whatsappNumber` as `telephone`, which asserts a voice line; `contactPoint` with `contactType: "customer service"` is the accurate shape for a WhatsApp-only channel.

findings.title: lastmod says every product changed on the same day
findings.detail: `lastmod: p.updatedAt`, with the comment at line 353 presenting importer churn as a feature: 'which the importers touch, so a re-import refreshes it'. All three importers `deleteMany` + `createMany` their whole source (CLAUDE.md, 'Importers are scoped by source'), so `updatedAt` is the import timestamp for every row. The sitemap therefore tells crawlers that all ~1,675 products changed simultaneously and none has changed since — which is false in both directions, and burns the crawl budget the file exists to direct. Either omit `lastmod` for importer-owned rows (as the category entries already honestly do, line 363's sibling at 362) or carry a content hash so only genuinely changed products advertise a new date.

findings.title: Trailing-slash URLs serve 200 with a second self-referential canonical
findings.detail: `canonical = origin + pathname`, and `pathname.split("/").filter(Boolean)` treats `/product/foo/` identically to `/product/foo`. So both URLs answer 200 with the same content and *different* self-referential canonicals, while the sitemap lists only the unslashed form — a duplicate pair that canonicalisation is specifically supposed to prevent. Same for `/category/foo/` and every STATIC path. One-line fix: normalise `pathname` (strip a trailing slash) before building `canonical`, or 301 to the canonical form.

findings.title: Product JSON-LD publishes one image and omits the recommended Offer fields
findings.detail: `images: { orderBy: { sortOrder: "asc" }, take: 1 }` means the JSON-LD `image` array (line 209) always has exactly one entry, though Beesline ships 555 images for 308 products and Dali 182 for 37 — Google explicitly asks for multiple images and multiple aspect ratios. The Offer (215-227) also omits `itemCondition` (`NewCondition` is checkable), `shippingDetails` and `hasMerchantReturnPolicy` — both of which the store CAN state from data it already holds (`DeliveryArea` fees, `freeDeliveryThresholdCents`, the settings-driven returns copy) and both of which Google now warns on. The Product node has no `url`/`@id`. Do NOT invent `priceValidUntil`, `gtin` or `sku` to silence the remaining warnings — the first is unknowable here and the last two are the rule this file was written to protect.

findings.title: apply-brand-allowlist prints reversal instructions naming a script that does not exist
findings.detail: After hiding products it logs 'Reversible: edit prisma/brands-we-sell.txt and run scripts/restore-brand.ts <name>.' There is no `scripts/restore-brand.ts` anywhere in the repo (only `restore-drill.ts`, which is the pg_restore drill). Combined with `applyBrandAllowlist` only ever writing `hidden` and never restoring, the true reversal is 'add the name back and re-run that source's importer' — which also recreates every row. An operator following the printed instruction gets a file-not-found and no way back. This is the same rule the codebase applies to the storefront ('a cleanup message must report the outcome, not the plan') applied to operator output.

findings.title: The SKU privacy check samples one arbitrary row and can fail spuriously
findings.detail: `db.product.findFirst({ where: { status: "active", NOT: { sku: "" }, images: { some: {} } } })` has no `orderBy`, so Postgres may return a different row per run — the assertion at line 81 then proves 'this one product's sku is not in its own page', which is a statement about one of ~1,675 products, not about the serialiser. It is also a raw `String.includes` against the whole HTML document, so a short sku (the catalogue contains 4-character ones such as `H234`) can collide with a Vite asset hash and produce a false FAIL — noise that trains the next reader to discount the suite, which CLAUDE.md already names as the failure mode that matters. Stronger form: assert structurally over a batch — fetch N product pages and their `/api/products/:slug` responses and check each against its own sku with a word-boundary match — and separately assert no `ProductImage.url` contains its product's sku (see the image-filename finding, which this check is currently blind to).

surveys.summary: The only order-change mechanism that exists is `POST /api/admin/orders/:id/resolve` with `action: "remove"` (server/src/index.ts:2192–2286) — it drops one pre-recorded blocked line and recomputes subtotal, delivery, coupon, points and gift card server-side, then best-effort re-prices the pending loyalty earn. There is no swap, no quantity change, no add-item, and no generic order editor anywhere in the server or admin UI; `accept` (substitute) changes status only and the confirm dialog tells the operator to "edit the order after confirming" via a surface that does not exist. The remove path also re-validates the coupon instead of re-pricing it, so an order that consumed a `maxUses` coupon or whose coupon has since expired silently loses its own discount, and it caps `pointsDiscountCents` down without writing any redemption reversal — the two drift bugs already patched in that block (the tier delivery perk, the gift-card refund) are the same shape and confirm the design is a second, hand-rolled copy of checkout's pricing with no shared function and zero HTTP-level test coverage.

findings.title: No mutation exists for swapping an item or changing a quantity — only removal
findings.detail: `POST /api/admin/orders/:id/resolve` accepts exactly three actions: `accept`, `remove`, `cancel` (index.ts:2179, 2185, 2192). The only order-item write anywhere outside checkout is `db.orderItem.delete` at index.ts:2261 — a repo-wide grep for `orderItem.create|update|upsert` finds nothing but the importers nulling `productId`. `adminApi` exposes only `setOrderStatus`, `askCustomer`, `resolveOrder` (web/src/admin/adminApi.ts:243–248). So for a business where the owner sources per order and confirms every order on WhatsApp, the daily operations 'swap this for that', 'make it 2 instead of 3' and 'add one more' have no code path at all. The one supported change also requires the item to have been pre-registered via `POST /orders/:id/awaiting` first — you cannot remove a line without first moving the whole order into `awaiting_customer` and naming that line.

findings.title: The coupon is re-VALIDATED, not re-priced — an order loses its own single-use or expired coupon on removal
findings.detail:
The remove path calls `evalCoupon(order.couponCode, subtotal)` (index.ts:2209). `evalCoupon` (index.ts:890–899) has four rejection branches and three of them are wrong at re-price time:

- `if (c.maxUses != null && c.usedCount >= c.maxUses)` (line 895) — checkout ALREADY claimed this order's use by incrementing `usedCount` (index.ts:1023–1026). For a `maxUses: 1` coupon this is guaranteed to fire, so the order is denied the coupon it already paid a use for.
- `if (c.expiresAt && c.expiresAt.getTime() < Date.now())` (line 894) — an order placed on the last day of a promo and sourced the next day loses its discount.
- `if (!c || !c.active)` (line 893) — deactivating a coupon in admin retroactively strips it from every in-flight order that used it.

Only the `subtotal < c.minOrderCents` branch (line 896) is the intended behaviour, and it is the only one the confirm dialog warns about (web/src/admin/AdminOrders.tsx:406–409). Concretely: order of $70 with WELCOME10-style `maxUses: 1`, $7 off, total $63. Remove a $10 line → subtotal $60, `discount` comes back 0, new total $60 + delivery instead of $53 + delivery. The customer's total goes UP by $7, `usedCount` is never decremented so the use stays consumed, and `Order.couponCode` is left populated (index.ts:2266 writes `discountCents` but not `couponCode`) while the admin breakdown hides the coupon line because it renders only when `discountCents > 0` (AdminOrders.tsx:278). The shop keeps the coupon use and the money.

findings.title: Points are capped down on removal with no redemption reversal — the customer's points evaporate
findings.detail: `const pointsDiscount = Math.min(order.pointsDiscountCents, Math.max(0, subtotal - discount));`. The comment above it (index.ts:2222–2234) correctly establishes that points already spent stay spent, but the `Math.min` silently reduces the applied discount when the surviving merchandise is worth less than the points already redeemed, and nothing gives the difference back. The `redeem` ledger entry written by `redeemWithin` is untouched, and `reverseRedemption` (server/src/loyalty/ledger.ts:647) is called only from `onOrderStatusChanged` for cancelled/refused/unavailable (hooks.ts:177–181) — never from the remove path. Failure: order subtotal $60, 300 points redeemed for $9, total $51. The $55 line cannot be sourced and is removed → subtotal $5, `pointsDiscount = min(900, 500) = 500`. The customer paid 300 points and receives $5 of value; ~133 points of value vanish with no entry explaining it. Compare the gift card two blocks down (index.ts:2254–2257), which does exactly the right thing with an `increment` refund and a history line — the same treatment was not extended to points. The in-code justification points at 'the note in the morning document about the case where removing an item leaves less merchandise than the points already covered', and MORNING.md contains no such note.

findings.title: The 'accept a substitute' resolution updates none of the three — and its dialog names an editor that does not exist
findings.detail: `if (action === "accept")` writes `status: "confirmed"` plus the awaiting-clear and an event, and nothing else (index.ts:2179–2183). Money: unchanged — the order still carries the unsourceable item's name, price and qty, so the customer is billed for a product they are not receiving and the driver's sheet (server/src/dispatch.ts:122, `itemsFaceValueCents`) describes a bag whose contents do not match. Points: unchanged — no `repricePendingEarn` call, so the pending earn is priced on the original basket. Customer total: unchanged. The confirm dialog concedes the gap in as many words: "Use this when the customer took an alternative at the same price. If the price differs, edit the order after confirming." (web/src/admin/AdminOrders.tsx:398) — there is no order editor in `web/src/admin/` and no endpoint behind one. This is the swap case, and today it is handled by pretending the price did not change.

findings.title: The 'Can't source an item' button is offered on five statuses where the server always rejects it
findings.detail: The button renders whenever `order.status !== "awaiting_customer" && !terminal`. `POST /orders/:id/awaiting` gates on `canTransition(order.status, "awaiting_customer")` (server/src/index.ts:2149), and server/src/status.ts:35–55 permits `awaiting_customer` only from `received`, `confirming`, `sourcing` and `on_hold`. So on `confirmed`, `packed`, `dispatched`, `out_for_delivery` and `delivered` the button is visible, opens a dialog, makes the operator pick an item and type a required note, and then 400s with 'Cannot ask the customer from “Confirmed”.' This directly violates the rule CLAUDE.md records for this screen — 'The UI offers only legal moves and the server independently rejects the rest' — which is honoured by the status Combobox (line 209–212) and not by this button. It also means the change flow is structurally unavailable at exactly the point the owner works: an order is `confirmed` or `packed` when the WhatsApp confirmation happens, and from `confirmed` the operator must first detour through `sourcing` to reach the flow at all; from `packed` there is no route back.

findings.title: Order pricing is implemented twice with no shared function, and has already drifted twice
findings.detail: Checkout prices an order at index.ts:1017–1146 (inside `placeOrder`); the remove path re-implements the same six-step arithmetic at index.ts:2198–2238. Nothing is shared — a grep for a pricing helper across `server/src` finds none; `freeDeliveryThresholdCents` is read independently at 951 and 2203, and the ordering rule (coupon → points → delivery → gift card) is written out twice. The two large comments inside the second copy are both post-mortems of that duplication: the tier free-delivery perk was missing so removal re-charged Bloom/Bouquet customers a fee their tier had earned (index.ts:2211–2217), and `pointsDiscountCents` was not written so the total stopped subtracting points the ledger still showed as spent (index.ts:2222–2234). This is the exact `rules.ts`/`ledger.ts` failure mode CLAUDE.md says the loyalty module was rebuilt to eliminate — two files each self-consistent and disagreeing with each other. Adding swap and quantity mutations on the current shape means a third and fourth copy.

findings.title: No test touches any order-mutation endpoint
findings.detail: A grep for `admin/orders` across `server/scripts/*.mjs` returns nothing, and no suite references `/resolve` or `/awaiting`. `test-checkout-money.mjs` covers placement only (delivery boundary, coupons, gift cards, races). The single piece of coverage in the whole change flow is `test-loyalty-hooks.mjs:291–316`, which calls `repricePendingEarn` directly with a hand-computed `halved` figure — it never exercises the HTTP path, so it cannot catch the coupon-revalidation bug, the points cap, or the gift-card refund arithmetic that sits between the endpoint and that function. This is the layer CLAUDE.md says the search-ranking defect lived in: 'Testing the search module alone passed the entire time.' The only mutation the shop has for changing a live order, on a database shared with production, is verified by nothing.

findings.title: The loyalty re-price is best-effort and nothing ever detects a miss
findings.detail: `await safely("reprice earn for order ${id}", () => repricePendingEarn(...))` runs AFTER the money transaction has committed (index.ts:2259–2284). `safely` (server/src/loyalty/hooks.ts:48–67) returns null on a 4s timeout or any throw, and logs to console only — 'There is no error-reporting service wired up'. So the money can commit while the points do not, and there is no reconciliation. Crucially the sweep cannot repair it: `load()` passes `merchandiseCentsOf(order)` into `computeState` (server/src/loyalty/ledger.ts:281–294), but `computeState` uses that map only for tier-spend via `countedMerchandise` (rules.ts:307–314) — the earn's `points` column is authoritative for the balance and is never re-derived from the order. A dropped re-price means the customer permanently earns on goods they did not receive, silently. Contrast the checkout hook, where a lost earn is recoverable from the admin ledger by hand; here nothing surfaces that the two are out of step.

findings.title: Nothing tells the customer the total changed
findings.detail: `queueMail` is called from exactly two places: checkout (index.ts:1195, order-confirmation carrying the placement total) and `PUT /orders/:id/status` (index.ts:2129). The resolve endpoint changes status on all three branches and the TOTAL on the remove branch, and queues no mail at all. Even if it did, `statusUpdateEmail` (server/src/mailer.ts:72) takes `(storeName, name, number, statusLabel, note)` and carries no money. The customer's own artefacts — the WhatsApp message they composed at checkout (web/src/pages/Checkout.tsx:115, `Total: ${usd(res.totalCents)}`) and the confirmation email — both hold the pre-change figure permanently. The new total reaches the customer only if they happen to reload /track, and reaches the door correctly only because `dispatch.ts` reads `order.totalCents` live. For a cash-on-delivery shop this is the doorstep argument `dispatch.ts` was written to prevent, arriving by a different route.

findings.title: The customer's tracking breakdown omits coupon, points and gift card, so it does not reconcile
findings.detail: The summary renders Subtotal, Delivery and Total only (Track.tsx:77–79). Any order with `discountCents`, `pointsDiscountCents` or `giftCardCents` set shows a subtotal and a total that differ by an unexplained amount — and after a remove that is precisely the state the customer is being asked to check. The server half of this fix landed and the client half did not: `GET /api/orders/:number` deliberately adds `pointsDiscountCents` to the redacted payload with the comment 'Without this the breakdown a customer sees on the tracking page does not add up' (server/src/index.ts:1500–1503), and `discountCents`/`giftCardCents` are in the allowlist too (line 1499). MORNING.md:233 flags the original gap. Account order history is thinner still — web/src/pages/Account.tsx:85 prints `totalCents` alone.

findings.title: The 50% redemption cap is silently exceeded after a removal
findings.detail: `RATES.redeemMaxShareOfMerchandise = 0.5` (server/src/loyalty/config.ts:67) is enforced at checkout by `previewRedemption`, which refuses with the customer-facing string 'Points may cover at most 50% of the items.' (server/src/loyalty/rules.ts:542, 572–573). The remove path caps `pointsDiscount` at `subtotal - discount` — 100% of the surviving merchandise, not 50%. Order of $100 with $50 redeemed (exactly at cap); remove a $40 line → subtotal $60, points still cover $50, i.e. 83%. The rule the shop states publicly is not re-checked by the one path that can invalidate it. Whichever direction is chosen — re-cap and reverse the surplus, or grandfather it — it should be a decision written down rather than a `Math.min` bound that happens to be the wrong one.

findings.title: A money-changing resolution records no operator reason
findings.detail: `await adminApi.resolveOrder(id, action, "")` — the note is hardcoded empty, and none of the three ConfirmDialogs (lines 394–417) contains an input for one. The server reads `str(req.body.note).trim()` (index.ts:2172) and falls back to canned text such as 'Removed “X” at the customer's request. Total recalculated.' So the order history can never say what the customer actually agreed to. `POST /orders/:id/awaiting` requires a note and refuses without one ('Say what you asked the customer — it is shown on the order.', index.ts:2152), and loyalty adjustments enforce `RATES.minAdjustmentReasonLength` (server/src/loyalty/admin.ts:291–297) — the one operation that rewrites an order's total is the one with no reason attached.

findings.title: `couponCode` and `giftCardCode` survive on the order after their amounts are zeroed
findings.detail: The remove update writes `subtotalCents, discountCents, giftCardCents, pointsDiscountCents, deliveryCents, totalCents` but leaves `couponCode` and `giftCardCode` as they were (index.ts:2264–2268). When a coupon is dropped (see the evalCoupon finding) or a gift card is fully refunded, the order keeps a code whose amount is now 0. Every consumer hides the line on the amount rather than the code — admin detail at web/src/admin/AdminOrders.tsx:278 and :289, dispatch's `whyDifferent` at server/src/dispatch.ts:83–85 — so nothing is displayed wrongly today, but the row records a promotion that was applied to nothing, which is the shape of thing a later query or export will read as truth.

surveys.summary: The reusable matcher lives in server/prisma/import-feel22.ts:218-253 (symmetric Jaccard ≥ 0.8 over brand-prefix-and-volume-stripped title tokens, gated by a bundle-only-matches-bundle rule) and is applied once, at import time, in one direction only at lines 363-392. Replaying that exact algorithm offline against the committed feeds shows it misses three whole classes: all 9 Dali duplicates never get compared at all (feed vendor "Dali Cosmetics" slugifies to `dali-cosmetics`, the direct brand slug is `dali`, so the candidate lookup at line 378 returns undefined), 24 genuine Beesline pairs score 0.50-0.75 and pass through, and 97 candidate intra-feel22 pairs among the 1,594 allowlisted rows are never looked for. The mundane checks are already half-built in `GET /api/admin/catalogue-health` (server/src/index.ts:2325-2352); the gaps are no upper price bound, an image count that measures database rows rather than renderable files, and no name validation on the product-update path.

findings.title: THE REUSABLE ALGORITHM — feel22 dedupe, precise enough to reimplement
findings.detail:
Lift this verbatim; do not reinvent it. Five pieces, all in import-feel22.ts:218-253.

1. CONSTANTS (233-234)
   MATCH_THRESHOLD = 0.8
   STOP = {the, and, for, with, new, free, pack, offer, special}

2. normaliseTitle(s, brand) (237-244), in this order:
   a. strip a leading brand prefix, anchored and case-insensitive, brand regex-escaped:
      new RegExp("^\\s*" + escapeRe(brand) + "\\s*", "i")
   b. .replace(/\(\s*\d+\s*\+\s*\d+[^)]*\)/g, " ")                          -> kills "(1+1 Free)"
   c. .replace(/\b\d+(\.\d+)?\s*(ml|l|g|gm|gr|mg|oz|pcs|caps|tabs)\b/gi, " ") -> kills "200ml", "50 g"
   d. .replace(/\b\d+\b/g, " ")                                             -> kills bare numbers

3. tokens(s, brand) (245-246): normaliseTitle -> lowercase -> /[^a-z0-9 ]+/g to spaces -> split on whitespace -> keep tokens with length > 2 that are not in STOP -> Set.

4. jaccard(a, b) (247-252): SYMMETRIC. i = |a n b|; union = a.size + b.size - i; return union ? i/union : 0. Two empty sets score 0, not 1.
   WHY NOT CONTAINMENT (the load-bearing history, 225-228): containment scores a short title fully inside a longer one at 1.0, so "Everyone Barrier Cream + Super Hydrating Serum" matched plain "Everyone Barrier Cream". It would have destroyed 156 rows instead of skipping 54.

5. isBundle(s) (253): /[A-Za-z)]\s+\+\s+[A-Za-z]/ tested AFTER the (1+1) marker is stripped — "1+1" is the same product twice, an offer, not a bundle.

THE PASS ITSELF (363-392):
   - load candidates: db.product.findMany({ where: { source: { in: ["dali","beesline"] } }, select: { name, brand: { slug, name } } })
   - BLOCK BY BRAND: bucket candidates into directByBrand keyed by brand.slug; candidates with no brand are dropped (line 371). This is what keeps it O(n * small) instead of 9,327 x 345.
   - for each feed product: cands = directByBrand.get(slugify(p.brand)); pt = tokens(p.title, p.brand); pBundle = isBundle(p.title)
   - for each candidate: `if (c.bundle !== pBundle) continue;` (383) then `if (jaccard(pt, c.toks) >= 0.8)` (384) -> record and break.
   - the action is SKIP, not delete (415): the losing row is never created. Nothing is ever deleted.

slugify is at 199-201: NFD, strip combining marks, lowercase, /[^a-z0-9]+/ -> "-", trim dashes, fallback "brand".

For a sweep over rows already in the database, the only substitutions needed are: iterate Product rows instead of feed records, use p.name instead of p.title and p.brand.name instead of p.brand, and block by brandId (or by a normalised brand key — see the Dali finding) instead of by slug.

findings.title: BLOCKER: the Dali half of the dedupe has never executed — brand slug mismatch
findings.detail:
`const cands = p.brand ? directByBrand.get(slugify(p.brand)) : undefined; if (!cands) continue;`

directByBrand is keyed by the DIRECT product's `brand.slug` (line 373). The Dali importer creates that brand as slug "dali" (server/prisma/import-dali.ts:231-235). Feel22's feed calls the vendor "Dali Cosmetics", and slugify("Dali Cosmetics") = "dali-cosmetics". The map lookup misses, `continue` fires, and NOT ONE of the 9 Dali comparisons is ever performed. Verified by grepping the feed: 9 rows with "brand":"Dali Cosmetics", 97 with "brand":"Beesline" — which is exactly the split the importer's own header comment claims to handle (line 25).

Both names sit on the allowlist (prisma/brands-we-sell.txt has BOTH "Dali" and "Dali Cosmetics"), so both sets are live on the storefront right now. The concrete damage: the direct Dali listing "Lip Butter Balm" carries 9 shade variations (Cherry Glaze, Cotton Candy, Peach Sorbet, Raspberry Jam, Salted Caramel, Strawberry, Vanilla Cake, Watermelon Sugar, Pink Meringue). The feel22 feed lists those same 9 shades as 9 SEPARATE products ("Dali Lip Butter Balm Peach Sorbet", etc.). Ten listings for one product.

Fix: a brand-alias map (feed vendor name -> direct brand slug) consulted before the lookup, or key directByBrand by a normalised brand token set rather than an exact slug. An alias table is the honest one — "Dali Cosmetics" and "Dali" being the same company is a fact nobody can derive from the strings.

Sibling hunt: this is the only cross-source name divergence in the current data — grep of the feed shows Beesline is spelled "Beesline" on both sides. But the failure is silent by construction (a missing map key produces no log line, no count, no error), so the alias map should also assert that every direct brand slug is reachable from at least one feed vendor name, and print the ones that are not.

findings.title: HIGH: 24 genuine Beesline duplicates score below 0.8 and are live on the storefront
findings.detail:
I replayed the exact algorithm (all five pieces above) offline against server/prisma/feel22-catalogue.json and server/prisma/beesline-catalogue.json — no database touched. 97 feed rows carry vendor "Beesline". Matches by threshold: >=0.8 -> 54, >=0.7 -> 60, >=0.6 -> 72, >=0.5 -> 78.

So 54 are skipped and 24 more real duplicates in the 0.50-0.75 band go straight into the catalogue. Every one I read is genuine (score, feel22 title, direct title):

  0.75  Beesline Express Facial Lifting Mask            <- Facial Lifting Mask
  0.75  Beesline Kids Sunscreen Cream Spf50 60ml        <- Kids Cream SPF50
  0.75  Beesline Express 9 Oils Hair Mask               <- Hair 9 Oils Mask
  0.75  Beesline Whitening Roll-On Deodorant            <- Whitening Roll-on Deodorant - Fragrance-Free
  0.75  Beesline 3 in 1 Micellar Cleansing Water        <- 3in1 Micellar Cleansing Water - 750ml
  0.67  Beesline 100% Natural Lip Balm - Chocolate & Orange  <- 100% Natural Lip Balm - Choco Orange (1+1)
  0.60  Beesline Ultrascreen Cream Active Protection SPF50   <- Ultrascreen Active SPF50
  0.60  Beesline Pure Carrot Suntan Oil SPF10 200 ML    <- Carrot Suntan Oil
  0.50  Beesline Whitening Facial Glow Toner            <- Whitening Toner
  0.50  Beesline Honey Moisturizing Soap - Fragrance Free   <- Honey Soap
  ... 14 more.

The losses are all the same shape: the direct listing is the SHORT clean name and feel22's is the long marketing one, so the extra tokens ("express", "pure", "perfect radiance", "cream", "active protection") inflate the union. That is precisely the case containment would have caught and is precisely why containment was rejected — which is why the answer is not "lower the threshold", it is a second, narrower rule (next finding) plus a reviewed list.

Recommendation: do NOT drop MATCH_THRESHOLD globally. Keep 0.8 as the auto-skip bar and emit a REVIEW band at 0.5-0.8 into a dry-run report the owner confirms once. 24 rows is a ten-minute job; 0.6 across the whole catalogue is 554 pairs and would be abandoned.

findings.title: HIGH: a title matcher structurally cannot see a variants-vs-rows duplicate
findings.detail:
Even with the brand-key bug fixed, the Dali case still does not fire. Simulated with the correct brand mapping: the 9 "Dali Lip Butter Balm <shade>" feed rows against the 37 direct Dali names score at most j = 0.60 against "Lip Butter Balm" (8 of 9 score 0.50). Nothing reaches 0.8, or even 0.7.

The reason is not fuzziness, it is granularity: one direct Product with 9 ProductVariant rows versus 9 Product rows. Jaccard over titles is being asked a question about the shape of the data, and it has no way to answer.

The rule that does answer it, and its guards:
  - same brand (after aliasing), AND
  - the DIRECT product has variants and the FEED product does not, AND
  - tokens(direct.name) is a strict SUBSET of tokens(feed.title), AND
  - the residual tokens (feed minus direct) match a variant label on the direct side.

That last clause is what makes this safe. It is the containment shape rejected at line 225-228, and it is only admissible because the residue must NAME something the direct product already sells. "Everyone Barrier Cream + Super Hydrating Serum" cannot pass it: the residue "super hydrating serum" is not a variant label of "Everyone Barrier Cream", and the bundle guard at 383 still applies. Keep both guards; dropping either reopens the 156-row hole.

Verification data if you build it: direct "Lip Butter Balm" variations are [Cherry Glaze, Cotton Candy, Peach Sorbet, Raspberry Jam, Salted Caramel, Strawberry, Vanilla Cake, Watermelon Sugar, Pink Meringue] and the 9 feed residues are exactly those 9 strings. A perfect 9/9 is the assertion to write.

findings.title: HIGH: the number-stripping and 3-char token floor produce Jaccard 1.0 FALSE positives
findings.detail:
Two normalisation steps that are safe for the current cross-source use are dangerous for any wider reuse, and the evidence is in the live feed rather than hypothetical.

(a) `.replace(/\b\d+\b/g, " ")` (line 243) deletes the only distinguishing token of whole product families. Grouping the 9,381 feed rows by (vendor, token set): 59 groups covering 131 rows differ ONLY in digits — 14 of those groups are on the brand allowlist and therefore visible. Real examples that would merge at j = 1.0:
    Cosrx The Retinol 0.3 Cream        vs  Cosrx The Retinol 0.1 Cream        (different strengths)
    Medicube Azelaic Acid Shot 2000    vs  Medicube ... Shot 7500
    Beurer Hc 50 / Hc 55 / Hc 30 Hair Dryer                                   (three different dryers)
    Pupa Invisible Sunscreen Spray Spf 50  vs  ... Spf 15
    Clinique 3 Step Skin Type 2 Set    vs  Skin Type 3 Set
  Note the spacing decides: "SPF50" survives as one token (no word boundary before the 5) while "Spf 50" loses its tier. Two products that mean the same thing normalise differently.

(b) `w.length > 2` (line 246) drops 1- and 2-character tokens. Confirmed collisions at j = 1.0:
    Flormar BB Cream  vs  Flormar CC Cream            -> both reduce to {cream}
    Lancome Renergie H.C.F. Triple Serum  vs  Renergie C.R.X Triple Serum  -> both {renergie, triple, serum}

Why the live importer gets away with it: the direct Beesline and Dali catalogues happen to contain no SPF-tier or numbered-shade families, so no false positive has ever had a candidate to hit. That is luck, not design — the same shape as the Windows file lock recorded in verify-sources.mjs.

Fix before reusing this for intra-feed or manual-source matching: keep numeric tokens that are NOT immediately followed by a volume unit (step (c) at line 242 already removed those), and lower the token floor to length >= 2. Then re-verify the 54 Beesline matches still all fire — that is the regression test.

findings.title: MEDIUM: the check runs once, at import, in one direction — nothing ever re-examines existing rows
findings.detail:
Three separate reasons it cannot catch everything, independent of any threshold:

1. ONE DIRECTION. Line 364-367 queries `source in ["dali","beesline"]` as candidates and feel22 as the subject. import-dali.ts and import-beesline.ts contain no comparable pass — grep for jaccard/dedupe/duplicate in both files returns only an unrelated comment about supplier product_type values. So the guarantee is "feel22 does not add a twin of something already there", never "the catalogue holds no twins".

2. ORDER-DEPENDENT AND UNENFORCED. CLAUDE.md:75 says "run Feel22 last". Nothing checks. Re-run `npm run import:beesline` after feel22 and beesline's 308 rows are deleted and recreated (import-beesline.ts:266) while feel22's twins sit untouched — no comparison runs, because the comparison lives in the other importer. Any product the Beesline supplier ADDS later whose feel22 twin already exists is permanently unreconciled.

3. SKIP, NOT SWEEP. The action is `continue` at line 415 — the row is never created. There is no code path anywhere that examines rows already in the Product table. So every duplicate created before the matcher existed, every one missed by a threshold or a brand-key bug, and every one introduced by the Excel importer (server/src/index.ts:2700-2749, which sets no `source` at all and upserts on slugify(brand + name), so "Dali Cosmetics"+name and "Dali"+name are two different rows) is invisible forever.

The sweep should therefore be a standalone dry-run script, not a fourth importer hook. Model it on server/scripts/apply-brand-allowlist.ts: dry run by default, `--write` to act, prints the full projection first, refuses to proceed when its own inputs do not reconcile, and never deletes (status change to `hidden` is the reversible move — and deleting an importer-owned row is undone by the next import anyway, the lesson already recorded in CLAUDE.md:449 and warned about in the admin delete dialog).

findings.title: MEDIUM: duplicates WITHIN a single feed are not looked for at all
findings.detail:
The skip loop only ever compares feed-to-direct. Two rows of the same feed are never compared to each other, and the feed contains plenty.

Measured over the 1,594 allowlisted feel22 rows (the ones that are actually visible), blocked by vendor: 24 pairs at j = 1.0, 27 at >= 0.9, 97 at >= 0.8, 195 at >= 0.7, 554 at >= 0.6. The j >= 0.8 list is 97 pairs — a reviewable morning, and it reuses the existing threshold so no new number has to be justified.

Genuine examples found at 1.0:
    Nivea Soft Cream  ||  Nivea Soft Cream            (identical title, two product_ids: 1720041766958 under "Day and Night Cream", 7838532501642 under "Body Lotion and Oil")
    Kiehl's Ultra Facial Cream 28ml  ||  Kiehl's Ultra Facial Cream
    Collistar Magic Drops Self-Tanning Concentrate 50ml  ||  ... Concentrate
    Garnier Ultra Doux Camomile Conditioner  ||  ... Conditioner - 200ml

But the same list also contains the Flormar BB/CC and Lancome H.C.F./C.R.X false positives above, so an intra-feed sweep MUST have the numeric/short-token fix applied first or it will propose merging different products. Run it as review-only output; never auto-hide.

Also not compared: dali-to-beesline. Those two catalogues share no brand, so the brand blocking would find nothing — I checked and there are no cross-brand candidates. Recording it as "none found" per the standing sibling-hunt rule rather than leaving it unstated.

findings.title: MUNDANE CHECK 1 — active products with no image
findings.detail:
THE QUERY ALREADY EXISTS. server/src/index.ts:2329 in GET /api/admin/catalogue-health:

    const visible = { status: { in: ["active", "unavailable"] } };
    db.product.count({ where: { AND: [visible, { images: { none: {} } }] } })

and the clickable filter that reproduces it exactly is `visible=1&hasImage=0` (line 2341), served by index.ts:1757 (`{ images: { none: {} } }`) and 1729. Reuse both; do not write a new one — the two agreeing is the reason the count is clickable.

Threshold: ZERO. This is not a tolerance band. Feed evidence: beesline 0 rows with no images, dali 0, feel22 7 — of which exactly 1 is both visible and on the brand allowlist ("Lattafa Sheikh Shuyukh Supreme Eau De Parfum"). Any number above single digits means an importer's image step failed, not that suppliers are sloppy.

THE GAP WORTH REPORTING: this counts ProductImage ROWS, not renderable files. web/src/lib/img.ts:41-46 rewrites /products/<src>/<file>.<ext> to /i/<slot>/<src>/<file>.webp with no existence check, and hasDerivative (49-51) tests the URL SHAPE only. If web/scripts/image-build.mjs could not process a source (it flags "FAILED to process" at line 197 and writes no derivative), the product has an image row, passes this query, and renders the fallback glyph. IMAGE-SUSPECTS.txt currently lists 2 such files. I traced both: LipContourLipStainFor12-HourWearRosewood.png (Huda Beauty, active, 13 images) and Packshotstemp-Lynn_*.png (MAC, hidden, its only image). Both brands are OFF the allowlist today, so the current visible exposure is 0 — but the comment at web/src/components/ProductImage.tsx:26-30 records that one of them was an active product's only image before the allowlist landed, and adding either brand back re-creates that. Add a second check that intersects visible products' image URLs against the derivative files on disk; it is a directory listing, not a query.

findings.title: MUNDANE CHECK 2 — zero or absurd prices (no upper bound exists anywhere)
findings.detail:
THE ZERO CHECK EXISTS: index.ts:2331, `db.product.count({ where: { AND: [visible, { priceCents: { lte: 0 } }] } })`, filter `visible=1&priceMax=0` (2343). Keep it, threshold ZERO. Feed evidence says it should read 0 today: every zero-price row in all three feeds is already forced to `hidden` by its supplier quality flag (feel22 price_zero -> hidden via productStatus at import-feel22.ts:204-208; beesline's 6 zero-price rows likewise). A non-zero count therefore means a manually created or Excel-imported row, which is the useful signal.

THERE IS NO UPPER BOUND ANYWHERE. Add one. Grounded thresholds, measured from the feeds rather than guessed:
  - dali: 37 products, $2.10-$6.50
  - feel22, allowlisted AND visible (1,560 rows): min > 0, exactly 1 row under $1.00, 21 rows in $1-$2, p50 $18.16, p99 $230, max $589 (Braun IPL PL5054). Only 4 rows above $300, all legitimate (Braun IPL, Oral-B iO 9, Lancome set, Bassam Fattouh box).
  - beesline (raw feed): max 767910 — Lebanese pounds left in after the store moved to USD. 24 rows above 1000, 13 at exactly 500.00 (placeholder), 6 at 0.00. All 43 are already `hidden`.

So:
  priceCents <= 0                 -> BLOCKER, expect 0
  priceCents < 100      ($1.00)   -> REVIEW. Currently returns exactly 1 row and it is a real error: "Nivea Soft Cream" at $0.21. Nothing legitimate is that cheap; even Dali's floor is $2.10.
  priceCents === 50000  ($500.00) -> the Beesline flat-placeholder fingerprint; an exact-equality check, worth its own line because it looks plausible.
  priceCents > 60000    ($600)    -> REVIEW. Above the real visible ceiling of $589. Returns 0 today, which is what makes it a usable alarm.
  priceCents > 100000   ($1,000)  -> BLOCKER, currency error. Any un-hidden Beesline LBP row lands here (767910 -> 76,791,000 cents).
Also worth adding, cheap: saleCents >= priceCents. Both write paths enforce sale < price (index.ts:1903 and 2728) so this only catches legacy rows, but it is one predicate.

findings.title: MEDIUM: basePrice takes the MINIMUM variant price, so one broken variant sets the listing price
findings.detail:
`basePrice` filters to variants with price_regular > 0, prefers the sellable ones, and returns Math.min over the pool. That is the mechanism behind the absurd-low price found above, and it is worth checking as its own class rather than only catching the output.

Worked example, feed product_id 1720041766958 "Nivea Soft Cream", variants:
    50ml=0.21  75ml=0.30  100ml=0.37  200ml=3.74  300ml=0.70   (all out_of_stock)
Min is 0.21, so the stored priceCents is 21 and the card advertises a Nivea Soft Cream for twenty-one cents. The 200ml at $3.74 is the only plausible figure in the row; the four small ones are supplier data errors, and taking the minimum guarantees the worst of them wins.

The detector: for each product, compare the cheapest and dearest priced variant. `max/min >= 10` with more than one priced variant is a supplier data error, not a size ladder — a 300ml is not 18x the price of a 50ml. Run it as a report over ProductVariant.priceCents joined to Product.priceCents; there is no need to change basePrice until the owner has seen the list.

findings.title: MUNDANE CHECK 3 — empty names, and the write path that can create one
findings.detail:
QUERY: `where: { AND: [{ status: { in: ["active","unavailable"] } }, { OR: [{ name: "" }, { name: { equals: " " } }] }] }` — or, since Prisma cannot express trim(), raw SQL: `SELECT id, slug, source FROM "Product" WHERE btrim(name) = '' AND status IN ('active','unavailable')`. Threshold ZERO, with a review band at `length(btrim(name)) < 3` (the same floor web/src/lib/productName.ts:56 already uses when deciding a trimmed name is too short to be an improvement).

NONE OF THE THREE FEEDS CAN PRODUCE ONE — I checked all 9,726 records: 0 empty or under-3-character names in feel22, beesline or dali, and 0 feel22 titles under 8 characters. So this check is not about suppliers.

THE PATH THAT CAN: `admin.put("/products/:id")` at server/src/index.ts:1946-1965 does NOT validate the name. `admin.post("/products")` does — line 1938, `if (!str(b.name).trim() || !num(b.categoryId)) return 400`. The update handler goes straight to productData() (which does `name: str(b.name).trim()`, line 1899) and then db.product.update. Clearing the name field in the admin editor and saving writes name = "" with a 200 OK. The Excel importer is safe (index.ts:2712-2713 skips nameless rows).

So the finding has two halves: run the query to see whether it has already happened, and add the same one-line guard to PUT that POST already has. A check that can only ever find damage a fixable endpoint keeps causing is half a control.

findings.title: INFO: Product fields available for matching, and which are indexed
findings.detail:
Product, server/prisma/schema.prisma:59-130. Usable for duplicate detection:

  name        String  (62)  — the primary signal. @@index([name]) at 127.
  slug        String  @unique (61) — NOT a duplicate signal here, see the separate finding.
  sku         String  (63)  — supplier reorder code. Cross-source useless (each supplier's own numbering) but exact-match within a source is a hard identity, and it is ADMIN-ONLY: never serialise it, and never put it in JSON-LD (CLAUDE.md rule, asserted by scripts/test-seo.mjs).
  source      String  (68)  — "dali" | "beesline" | "feel22" | "" (manual/Excel). The partition the whole sweep is organised around. @@index at 124.
  brandId     Int?    (106) — the blocking key. @@index at 123. Nullable, and the current matcher silently drops null-brand candidates (import-feel22.ts:371).
  categoryId  Int     (104) — @@index at 122. A useful secondary guard: two products in unrelated departments are not the same product. Note departments hold no products directly, so any rollup must include children.
  priceCents  Int     (84)  — @@index at 125. A tie-breaker, not a matcher; the same product legitimately differs in price between a direct listing and a retailer.
  status      String  (83)  — active|hidden|unavailable|discontinued. @@index at 121. Scope the sweep to active+unavailable to match what a shopper sees.
  searchText  String  (99)  — ALREADY normalised: name + brand + category + parent + tags, accents folded, punctuation dropped, plus a space-stripped copy (server/src/search.ts:57-72). There is a GIN trigram index on it (server/src/searchIndex.ts:29-31), so `similarity(a."searchText", b."searchText")` gives a fast in-database pre-filter to generate candidate pairs before running the Jaccard rule in TypeScript. Best available accelerator if the sweep needs to scale past brand blocking. It is never serialised to anyone.
  shortDesc / description (86-87), concerns / attributes (100,102), images[] (111), variants[] (112), createdAt/updatedAt (116-117, indexed).

ProductVariant (146-160): type (shade|size), label, sku, hex, imageUrl, priceCents, available, sortOrder. `variants.length` is the field that makes the granularity rule possible. `available` is a per-shade flag, NOT a quantity — there is no stock anywhere in this schema and there must never be.
ProductImage (132-141): url, alt, sortOrder.

findings.title: INFO: slug collision is NOT a duplicate signal here — verified, none found
findings.detail:
Worth recording so nobody builds the sweep on it. import-feel22.ts:424-431 re-slugs a colliding handle to `<handle>-f22`, then `-f22-2` and so on, and counts it in `reslugged`. That counter looks like a free duplicate detector.

It is not. I compared the feeds directly: 0 of the 9,381 feel22 handles collide with any beesline handle (import-beesline.ts:295 uses `slug: p.handle`) or any dali slug (import-dali.ts:272 uses `slug: p.slug`), and there are 0 duplicate handles within the feel22 feed itself. So the re-slug branch has never executed and `reslugged` is always 0.

The reason is structural: each supplier mints handles in its own namespace, and the 9 Dali duplicates are "dali-lip-butter-balm-peach-sorbet" against a direct slug of "lip-butter-balm". Real duplicates do not collide on slug, so slug uniqueness provides no protection at all. Recording "none found" as information, per the standing sibling-hunt rule.

findings.title: INFO: three recorded figures for the same quantity disagree — resolve before publishing any sweep
findings.detail:
The repo's own rule ("a sum that does not reconcile is a confession", CLAUDE.md:929) applies to this feature's own documentation.

  CLAUDE.md:89     "54 products skipped"
  CLAUDE.md:95     "would have deleted 156 products instead of skipping 54"
  import-feel22.ts:228  "would have deleted 156 products instead of 80"
  import-feel22.ts:25   "Feel22 resells brands we already buy direct (97 Beesline, 9 Dali products)"

54 and 80 cannot both be the skip count. My offline replay of the exact algorithm resolves it: 54 at threshold 0.8, which is 54 of the 97 Beesline rows and 0 of the 9 Dali rows — the Dali zero being the brand-key blocker above. So CLAUDE.md is right and the code comment at line 228 is stale by 26.

This matters beyond tidiness: the next person sizing this work reads "80 of 106 already handled, 26 to go" when the truth is "54 of 106 handled, 52 to go", and sets the scope of the sweep from a wrong number. Correct line 228 to 54 as the first commit of the sweep, before any behaviour changes.
